title: 7.12 A horse can run fast
unit_title: Everyday needs, plans and free time
unit_outcome: Say what hurts and why someone feels a certain way, describe what people are wearing and the weather as it happens, tell someone to put on or take off clothes, talk about what people like doing, invite and answer, ask someone to repeat or explain, talk about being sick, the months and seasons, compare with the biggest and the tallest, and say what people and animals can do and are good at.
goal: Say what people and animals can and can't do (A horse can run fast. / A snake can't walk.) and ask Can you …? with Yes, I can. / No, I can't.
grammar_function: A follow-up of A1 7.12 Farm and Wild Animals: A1 names animals and what they are doing (The horse is running.); A1+ 7.12 says what they and the cast are able to do. The one new grammar relationship is can / can't + a verb for ability (A horse can run fast. / A snake can't walk. / Luis can't play tennis.), with Can you …? and the short answers Yes, I can. / No, I can't.; can't first came in A1+ 6.9 as not allowed (You can't park here.), and here it says not able. Can you pass …? (A1+ 5.14) asks someone to do something and is not used here. A1 7.12's horse, monkey and snake, 7.13's two new tennis photos and the cast's swimming and running photos show each answer.
prerequisite: A1 7.12 animals; A1 7.8 fast; A1 7.13 tennis and sing; A1+ 1.3 swim and run; A1+ 6.9 can't (not allowed); A1+ 7.13's tennis photos.
speaking_outcome: Say can as a weak kun before the verb (I kun SWIM) but full in the short answer (Yes, I CAN.); say can't with a long vowel and a clear t (KANT). Do not require native-like speed.
